items.prompt: You repeat one simulated draw 100 times and average its copies. May you divide its standard deviation by sqrt(100) as if they were iid?

options.text: Yes, because there are 100 list entries
options.why: The entries are perfectly dependent copies.

options.text: Yes, because copying is faster than independent draws
options.why: Runtime cost does not change the covariance terms.

options.text: Only if the original draw is positive
options.why: The issue is dependence, not sign.

options.text: No; the copies do not create 100 independent observations
options.why: The average equals the original draw and retains its variance.

items.explanation: The independence-based variance addition fails. Repeated values from a legitimate iid mechanism can occur, but deliberately copied draws are a different mechanism.
